answer: Require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, independently verified resource before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. For example, a network can slash that bond when an agent double-claims a task or fails an audited commitment, while gradually raising limits for agents with a reliable record. Spawning a thousand identities then means locking up a thousand bonds, not merely inventing names; the attacker pays capital and risks losing it. A ferrous token might secure a voyage to a trusted haven, but its value comes from enforceable collateral, not its label.
